The Katsina State Police Command on Thursday arrested 14 suspects over an attack on a convoy of All Progressives Congress supporters along the Yashi–Funtua road in Malumfashi Local Government Area of the state. The incident occurred on Wednesday, as the convoy was travelling through Malumfashi to Funtua for a campaign flag-off. The police said suspected political thugs armed with knives and stones attacked the convoy and passing commercial vehicles, smashing the windscreens of several vehicles and injuring a female motorist travelling in a commercial vehicle. This was contained in a statement by the state Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Abubakar Sadiq and made available to newsmen. Sadiq said police operatives deployed along the route responded swiftly to restore order and arrest the suspects. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The statement read, “The command had made adequate security arrangements and deployed personnel along key routes and identified locations, including the Yashi–Funtua road, ahead of the campaign event. “However, an unlawful assembly of suspected political thugs armed with knives and stones began hurling stones at the convoy of APC supporters and passing commercial vehicles.” It added that the attack resulted in damage to several vehicles and injuries to a female motorist. The command said efforts were ongoing to track down other suspects who fled the scene. The Commissioner of Police, Ali Umar Fage, condemned the attack and warned against political violence during the electioneering period. He said the command would not tolerate political thuggery or any conduct capable of threatening public peace before, during or after elections. “The command will not tolerate any form of political thuggery, violence, or actions capable of breaching public peace before, during, or after the electioneering period,” the statement quoted the commissioner as saying. The police said investigations into the incident were ongoing and promised to communicate further developments to the public. The attack occurred amid political campaign activities in Katsina State ahead of the 2027 general elections. Esha Aliku
